overview: Smart Building Indoor Comfort Monitoring addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in construction and real estate operations. The first proof of value uses room temperature, CO2 and occupancy readings. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is occupied hours outside comfort band, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: room temperature, CO2 and occupancy readings; define occupied hours outside comfort band and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Development Director / Property Operations Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
